solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Home again by tea time bringing sauce

parts.note: to be home again is to be back
cha is an informal word for tea

explanation.surface: Someone gets home in time for tea and brings along a bottle of sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' looks like a condiment brought home, but it means cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce in the sense of impudence is cheeky answering back, which is what this informal word for insolent retort means.

clue.text: Hope for one's changes to be made by sexton?

definitions.meaning: the comedian Bob Hope is one example of a Bob, and the possessive 's ends the word

definitions.text: changes to be made by sexton?
definitions.meaning: in church bell-ringing a bob is a call that alters the order in which the bells ring

explanation.surface: Someone hopes a church official will make some alterations.
explanation.walkthrough: A sexton was traditionally the church caretaker who rang the bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobs are standard variations in change-ringing of church bells, so they are changes a bell-ringing sexton makes.

clue.text: Wind and cold where surfers go?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
web surfers go to a URL, a web address

explanation.surface: Surfers head where the wind blows and the water is cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surfers are web surfers, not ones riding waves.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind something round is to coil or twist it, which is the verb sense of making a ringlet.

clue.text: As bill passed on involving millions, this certainly ….?

definitions.text: As bill passed on involving millions, this certainly ….?

parts.note: cos is an informal short form of because, which as can mean
a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab

indicators.note: involving means the letters for passed on take in the letter for millions

parts.note: OB stands for obiit, Latin for died, so passed on

explanation.surface: A bill involving millions has been passed on, so the job certainly cost plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a bill involving millions certainly cost a lot. OB, from Latin obiit, is the convention for died.
explanation.definitionFit: To cost a bomb is British slang for to be very expensive, which a bill running to millions plainly is.

clue.text: Heroine of rank an inane article rubbished

indicators.note: rubbished means trashed, so the letters are knocked about and rearranged

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A literary critic dismisses a silly piece about a heroine of high rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Karenina is the title heroine of Tolstoy's novel about an aristocrat's doomed affair.

clue.text: One that would catch pillow talk perhaps, after your blood?

definitions.text: One that would catch pillow talk perhaps
definitions.meaning: a listening device hidden in a bed would pick up what lovers say there
an insect living in mattresses that bites sleepers and feeds on their blood

explanation.walkthrough: Read one way it is a spy's microphone in the bedroom; read the other, the blood-sucking pest of mattresses.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug is both a hidden microphone and an insect, so the bedroom version fits both an eavesdropping device and a blood-feeding pest.

clue.text: Drama queen visiting much of Europe and America

indicators.note: visiting means the queen goes inside the letters for the European Union

parts.note: the EU, the European Union, covers much of Europe
US, the United States, is America, joined on by and

explanation.surface: A theatrical queen tours most of Europe and the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drama queen' looks like one phrase; 'Drama' is the definition and 'queen' the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Equus is Peter Shaffer's 1973 stage play about a boy who blinds horses.

clue.text: What we pay pub to host European party: a figure to toy with

indicators.note: to host means to take guests in, so the bill holds the other letters

parts.note: a bar bill is what drinkers owe the pub
a do is a party

explanation.surface: The pub charges for a European party and the evening's entertainment is a figure to play with.
explanation.definitionFit: This fashion figure made by Mattel is a plastic toy figure that children play with.

clue.text: Footballer outstanding at the back, awfully like a rock

indicators.note: at the back means the final letter of the word is taken
awfully means badly done, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A footballer who excels in defence is terribly solid, like a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding at the back' sounds like a star defender; it gives just the G at the back of 'outstanding'.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby and Australian football this is a player who takes the kicks at goal, a kind of footballer.

clue.text: Sentence that could be long? Therefore no good tweeting

parts.note: bird is British slang for a prison sentence, as in 'doing bird', and such a stretch can be a long one
so means therefore

explanation.surface: A judge wonders whether a long sentence is pointless, while birds chatter outside.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD as a prison term is British slang (from rhyming slang 'bird lime' = time).
explanation.definitionFit: Tweeting is the chirping of small songbirds, the very music this compound word names.

clue.text: Fur freak feeling rejected

parts.note: a freak, as in a fitness freak, is an enthusiast or nut

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the word for feeling is written backwards

parts.note: an air is a feeling or impression given off

explanation.surface: A fur-hating zealot feels spurned.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutria is the trade name for the pelt of the coypu, a South American rodent farmed for fur.

clue.text: Presumably thin sailor left in house, puzzling

parts.note: someone not fat is presumably thin

indicators.note: in means the sailor and left are placed inside the house

parts.note: a home is a house
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A slim sailor has been left at home, which is a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be fathomed or understood is baffling, puzzling.

clue.text: Support for constitutional edict backed: ruler to remain

indicators.note: backed means the word for edict is turned back to front

parts.note: an edict is a decree, a law
a king is a ruler
to stick is to stay or remain

explanation.surface: A monarch issues a decree to back the constitution and stays put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constitutional' suggests politics but is the noun: a health-giving stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A constitutional is a walk taken for one's health, and a cane carried on it gives the walker support.

clue.text: Fail to lift trophy? Pretend not to notice

indicators.note: in a down clue to lift is to raise up, so the word for trophy reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an award is a trophy or prize
to blank someone is to ignore them, pretending not to see them

explanation.surface: A team fails to lift the cup and its captain pretends not to have noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lift' turns AWARD upwards to give DRAWA. 'Fail to lift trophy' reads as one phrase; only 'Fail' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from pulling a losing lottery ticket, so it means to get nowhere, to fail.

clue.text: Northern town where a county council cut mobile phone signal

parts.note: CC is the abbreviation for county council

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: a ringtone is the sound a mobile phone makes to signal a call

explanation.surface: A northern town where the local council has cut off mobile phone reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the final E. Accrington is a Lancashire town in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Accrington is a mill town in Lancashire, in the north of England, famous for its football club Stanley.

clue.text: Page Three, perhaps, right to be hidden from vicar

indicators.note: something hidden from a word is taken out of it, so a letter disappears from the priest's title

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest like a vicar

explanation.surface: A tabloid's notorious Page Three must be kept away from the vicar's eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: The final R of RECTOR goes. 'Page Three' evokes the Sun's topless models; here it is just an odd-numbered page.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd-numbered pages of a book, such as page three, are right-hand pages, which printers call by this Latin term.

clue.text: Romantic chap going out with Doris

indicators.note: going out with someone is dating, but it also suggests the letters leave their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lovestruck man is dating a woman named Doris.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsodic means extravagantly enthusiastic and emotional, which matches romantic in the sense of effusive feeling.

clue.text: Desire this so-called lustre, etc — a ruby possesses it

definitions.note: the named thing in the play title, 'A ___ Named Desire'

indicators.note: possesses it means the run of words holds the answer within it

explanation.surface: A ruby is so lustrous it seems to have everything, glitter and all.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennessee Williams's play is 'A Streetcar Named Desire', so Desire is this, so called.
explanation.definitionFit: In New Orleans a tram line called Desire gave Tennessee Williams the title of his play about a tram so named.

clue.text: Sir comes in tired: check for purpose-built seat?

indicators.note: comes in means the knighthood is placed inside the word for tired

parts.note: worn means tired out
a KBE, Knight Commander of the British Empire, is addressed as Sir
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A weary knight wants a check that there is a proper seat waiting for him.
explanation.walkthrough: KBE is a British knighthood whose holder is called Sir.
explanation.definitionFit: A bench is a seat, and this one is built for the purpose of doing manual jobs on rather than for sitting.

clue.text: European poet's kind, touching hosts

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: hosts means the word for touching holds the word for kind inside it

parts.note: re means about or concerning, touching on
ilk means kind or sort

explanation.surface: A European poet is a kindly sort, moving to the people he entertains.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke was a Bohemian-Austrian poet writing in German, author of the Duino Elegies.

clue.text: Broken rubber in many bits of some value

indicators.note: broken means the letters of the phrase are smashed and put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A broken rubber has ended up in lots of pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bits' are not pieces but binary digits, the noughts and ones of computing.
explanation.definitionFit: A value written in base two is a string of binary digits, so it is bits that together have some value.

clue.text: Jack beams when picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for beams is said out loud

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Jack smiles broadly when someone gives him a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beams' looks like a verb for smiling, but it is the plural noun for shafts of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack a car up is to lift it with a jack, so jack means lift or hoist.

clue.text: Sting mouth: a hazard of course

definitions.meaning: a sting is an operation set up to catch criminals
slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your ...'
a bunker on a golf course is a sand hazard

explanation.surface: A wasp sting to the mouth is a hazard on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the golf course hazard is a sand bunker.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare is set to catch people out, slang uses it for the gob, and golf calls a sand bunker one too.

clue.text: Where couple covered up for PM once

definitions.meaning: Adam and Eve covered their nakedness with fig leaves in the Garden
Anthony, later Lord Avon, was British Prime Minister 1955 to 1957

explanation.surface: A former prime minister was where a pair of politicians hushed up a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister after Churchill, resigning after Suez.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam and Eve's garden is where they first clothed themselves, and Anthony Eden was a twentieth-century British prime minister.

clue.text: Foreign girl having legs round but short

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: astride means with legs on either side of something

explanation.surface: A girl from abroad sits with her legs around something but she is small.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrid is a Scandinavian girl's name, so to an English-speaking setter it marks a foreign girl.

clue.text: Alumni better out of sight?

parts.note: OBs, old boys, are former pupils of a school
to better a patient is to make them well, to cure them, so better here means made well

explanation.surface: Former pupils wonder whether it is better to stay out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscured is hidden from view, blocked from being seen.

clue.text: We hear boy's going to a best friend's place

indicators.note: we hear means what follows is said out loud and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: Ken is a boy's name, and Ken'll is short for Ken will, Ken is going to

explanation.surface: We are told a lad is off to visit his closest friend's home.
explanation.walkthrough: A dog is man's best friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog is called man's best friend, and the hut where a dog sleeps is its home.

clue.text: One shelled out to get a printer?

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hands out money to buy a printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelled out' reads as paid, but 'shelled' belongs to the definition and 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a freshwater turtle, a creature with a shell, so one that is shelled.
